- Overestimate prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is negative or near-zero (especially >3 consecutive days), reduce forecasted mean by 1–3% to account for downward pressure.
- After a price spike (e.g., >75.0), model tends to overshoot; cap forecasted peak at 10–15% below the spike’s high.
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum (e.g., >0.7 for 3+ days), model often overreacts; dampen forecast slope by 10–20% in the first 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is volatile or near-zero, avoid sharp upward trends; favor smoother, lower-variance trajectories.
- If true outcome shows early drop (e.g., first 3 days below 70), model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast by 2–5% in first 3 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
